zebralogic.title: Assign fixed‑position attributes immediately
zebralogic.principle: If a clue directly ties an attribute to a specific house number, place that attribute in that house right away and remove it from all other houses.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue mentions a concrete house index (e.g., "the person in the third house ...").
zebralogic.example: Incorrectly leaving the "bachelor" degree unassigned despite a clue that says "the bachelor lives in house 3".

zebralogic.title: Translate direct adjacency into offset constraints
zebralogic.principle: Clues using "directly left of" or "directly right of" impose an exact offset of one house; encode them as pos(A) = pos(B) − 1 or pos(A) = pos(B) + 1.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue contains "directly left of" or "directly right of".
zebralogic.example: Mis‑interpreting "the beach vacation is directly left of Arnold" as merely "beach is somewhere left of Arnold".

zebralogic.title: Interpret distance clues correctly
zebralogic.principle: A clue stating "N houses between X and Y" means the absolute positional difference is N + 1; there are exactly N houses separating them.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue mentions a specific number of houses between two attributes.
zebralogic.example: Treating "two houses between the Pall Mall smoker and mother Penny" as a distance of 2 instead of the correct distance of 3.

zebralogic.title: Bind equivalence clues to the same house
zebralogic.principle: When a clue equates two (or more) attributes, they must belong to the same house; assign them together and eliminate those values from all other houses.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses language like "is the same as", "also", "the X is the Y", etc.
zebralogic.example: Failing to place "Yellow Monster" cigar and "lime" smoothie together after the clue "the Yellow Monster smoker drinks lime smoothies".

zebralogic.title: Treat "somewhere left/right of" as inequality
zebralogic.principle: Clues that say X is somewhere to the left/right of Y impose only an ordering (pos(X) < pos(Y) or pos(X) > pos(Y)), without fixing distance or adjacency.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue contains "somewhere left of", "somewhere right of", "to the left of", or "to the right of" without "directly".
zebralogic.example: Interpreting "Peter is somewhere left of the lime smoothie drinker" as "Peter is directly left of" and fixing their positions incorrectly.

zebralogic.title: Apply exclusion constraints
zebralogic.principle: Clues that forbid an attribute from a particular house (e.g., "X is not in house Y") should be recorded as a negative placement, removing that possibility from the house.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue explicitly states that an attribute cannot be in a given house.
zebralogic.example: Ignoring the clue "Peter is not in the first house" and allowing Peter to occupy house 1.

zebralogic.title: Enforce uniqueness across each attribute category
zebralogic.principle: Each value in a category must appear exactly once; after assigning a value to a house, remove it from the candidate sets of all other houses in that category.
zebralogic.example: Assigning the "associate" degree to two different houses, violating the one‑per‑category rule.

zebralogic.title: Disambiguate overlapping attribute values across categories
zebralogic.principle: When a clue mentions a term that appears in more than one attribute category (e.g., "rabbit" in both Pet and Animal), use contextual words like "pet", "animal", "owner", or "keeper" to decide which category the clue applies to, and apply the constraint only to that category.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue contains a value that is present in multiple attribute categories.
zebralogic.example: Incorrectly treating the clue "the rabbit owner smokes blends" as referring to the Animal category, thereby assigning rabbit to Animal instead of to Pet.

zebralogic.title: Preserve original case of attribute values
zebralogic.principle: Attribute values must be output exactly as they appear in the problem statement, including capitalization; altering case (e.g., "Desert" vs "desert") leads to a mismatch even if the logical assignment is correct.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: During final answer generation, before emitting the JSON solution.
zebralogic.example: Outputting "Desert" for a Smoothie value when the puzzle lists the value as "desert", causing the verifier to reject the answer.

zebralogic.title: Interpret "next to each other" as bidirectional adjacency
zebralogic.principle: Clues stating that two entities are "next to each other" indicate they occupy adjacent houses, but do not specify which is left or right; enforce adjacency without assuming a direction.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses phrasing like "next to each other", "are adjacent", or "are side by side" without a directional qualifier.
zebralogic.example: Assuming the dog owner is left of the lime‑smoothie drinker in the clue "Dog owner and lime smoothie drinker are next to each other", rather than allowing either order.

zebralogic.description: Treating "somewhere left of" as adjacency (directly left)
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model conflates the vague ordering phrase with the stricter "directly left of" wording, leading to overly specific placements.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Remember that "somewhere left of" only imposes pos(X) < pos(Y); do not enforce an offset of one house.

zebralogic.description: Interpreting "N houses between" as distance N
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model forgets that the distance between the two houses is N + 1, counting the houses in between rather than the total span.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Add one to the stated number of houses when converting to positional difference.

zebralogic.description: Ignoring equivalence clues that bind two attributes to the same house
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model treats each attribute independently, missing the requirement that they share a house.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Whenever a clue equates two (or more) attributes, place them together and remove those values from all other houses.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model may assign the same value to multiple houses within a category, overlooking the global uniqueness constraint.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: After any placement, eliminate that value from the candidate sets of all other houses in the same category.

zebralogic.description: Assuming a fixed direction for "next to each other" clues
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model treats "next to each other" as "directly left of" or "directly right of", fixing an order that the clue does not specify.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Interpret such clues as bidirectional adjacency: enforce |pos(A) − pos(B)| = 1 without assigning left/right.
